_about: Study page (study.html): practice questions by exam, rendered by js/study.js. Each question has exactly 4 options, answer (the 0-based index of the right one) and why (one or two plain sentences). tests/study.test.mjs checks the shape.
note: A few sample questions per exam for now; more are coming.

exams.name: Security+
exams.about: CompTIA's entry-level security certification: threats, architecture, operations and governance.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of multifactor authentication?
options: A fingerprint and a face scan
A password and a code from an authenticator app
questions.why: Multifactor means factors of different kinds. A password is something you know and the app's code comes from something you have. The other pairs use the same kind twice.

questions.q: A company wants to detect whether a file was changed while it was being transferred. What should it use?
questions.why: A hash of the file is compared before and after the transfer; any change to the file changes the hash. That checks integrity. Encryption protects confidentiality instead.

questions.q: Which type of malware encrypts a victim's files and demands payment to unlock them?
questions.why: Ransomware holds data hostage by encrypting it. Spyware watches the user, a rootkit hides an attacker's presence, and a logic bomb runs when a set condition is met.

exams.name: Network+
exams.about: CompTIA's networking certification: addressing, routing and switching, wireless, troubleshooting and network security.

questions.q: How many usable host addresses does a /26 IPv4 subnet have?
questions.why: A /26 leaves 6 bits for hosts: 2 to the power of 6 is 64 addresses. Take away the network and broadcast addresses and 62 are usable.

questions.q: Which protocol automatically gives a device its IP address, subnet mask and default gateway?
questions.why: DHCP hands out addressing settings. DNS turns names into addresses, ARP finds the hardware address for an IP address, and NTP sets the clock.

questions.q: Which device's main job is to forward traffic between different IP networks?
questions.why: A router works at layer 3 and chooses a path between networks by IP address. A hub and a repeater only repeat signals, and an access point connects wireless devices to one network.

exams.name: CySA+
exams.about: CompTIA's security analyst certification: detection, vulnerability management and incident response.

questions.q: Logs show one source address failing to log in to hundreds of different accounts, trying the same password on each. What is this?
options: A brute-force attack on one account
questions.why: Password spraying tries one common password across many accounts, which avoids locking any single account. Credential stuffing replays known username and password pairs from a breach.

questions.q: A workstation is confirmed to have malware that is spreading to other machines. In the usual incident response order, what comes next?
questions.why: After detection and analysis comes containment: isolate the machine to stop the spread. Eradication, recovery and lessons learned follow in that order.

questions.q: What severity rating does a CVSS base score of 9.0 to 10.0 have?
questions.why: CVSS rates 9.0 to 10.0 as Critical, 7.0 to 8.9 as High, 4.0 to 6.9 as Medium and 0.1 to 3.9 as Low.

exams.name: PenTest+
exams.about: CompTIA's penetration testing certification: planning and scoping, reconnaissance, attacks and reporting.

questions.q: Before testing starts, which document sets out what the tester may and may not do, such as the targets, the allowed times and the methods?
questions.why: The rules of engagement define how the test is carried out and its limits. A non-disclosure agreement only covers confidentiality, and a service-level agreement covers service targets.

questions.q: Which Nmap option runs a TCP SYN ("half-open") scan?
questions.why: -sS sends a SYN and never completes the handshake. -sT is a full TCP connect scan, -sU scans UDP, and -sn finds live hosts without scanning ports.

questions.q: A tester collects employee names and email addresses from public websites, without sending anything to the target's systems. What is this called?
questions.why: Passive reconnaissance uses public sources and never touches the target. Scanning and enumeration send traffic to the target's systems, and exploitation uses a weakness.
